pinyin: jūn zǐ zhōu ér bù bì
natural: the gentleman is inclusive, not partisan

meaning.en: The gentleman is broad-minded and fair to all, and does not form cliques; the small man does the reverse.
meaning.zh: 君子以道义团结众人而不拉帮结派，小人则相反。

equivalents: fair to all, partial to none

examples.zh: 公司领导要君子周而不比，不能搞小圈子。
examples.en: Company leaders should be inclusive and avoid forming cliques.

examples.zh: “君子周而不比，小人比而不周”，用来形容办公室政治再合适不过。
examples.en: 'The gentleman is inclusive without cliquishness; the small man is cliquish without inclusiveness' fits office politics perfectly.

story.en: Confucius: 'The gentleman is inclusive and not partisan; the small man is partisan and not inclusive' (君子周而不比，小人比而不周).
story.zh: 《论语·为政》：“君子周而不比，小人比而不周。”

usage.en: Note 比 is read bì here ('to ally in a clique'), not bǐ 'compare'. Often quoted with its second half 小人比而不周.
usage.zh: 注意此处“比”读 bì，指结党营私，不读 bǐ。常与下句“小人比而不周”连用。

pinyin: jūn zǐ tài ér bù jiāo
literal: gentleman · at ease · yet · not · proud
natural: the gentleman is at ease but not arrogant

meaning.en: The gentleman is composed and dignified without being arrogant; the small man is arrogant without being at ease.
meaning.zh: 君子心胸坦荡安舒而不骄傲，小人骄傲却不安舒。

examples.zh: 他功成名就，却依然君子泰而不骄。
examples.en: Though successful and famous, he remains composed and without conceit.

examples.zh: 老前辈说，做人要君子泰而不骄，小人骄而不泰。
examples.en: The old master said: be at ease without pride, and avoid pride without ease.

story.en: Confucius: 'The gentleman is at ease but not arrogant; the small man is arrogant but not at ease' (君子泰而不骄，小人骄而不泰).
story.zh: 《论语·子路》：“君子泰而不骄，小人骄而不泰。”

usage.en: Quoted in advice on character and demeanour; the second half is 小人骄而不泰.
usage.zh: 常用于讲修养风度，下句为“小人骄而不泰”。

natural: when the root is set, the Way grows

meaning.en: Once the foundation is firm, the right course develops of itself; in the Analects, filial piety and respect for elders are the root of humaneness.
meaning.zh: 根本确立了，道理和事业自然产生；《论语》以孝悌为仁之本。

equivalents: get the foundation right and the rest follows
a firm root grows the Way

examples.zh: 学艺先练基本功，本立道生，不可急于求成。
examples.en: In learning a craft, drill the basics first; once the root is set the rest follows, so do not rush.

examples.zh: 企业文化是根本，本立道生，制度才能落地。
examples.en: Corporate culture is the root; when it is firm, rules take effect.

story.en: Youzi says: 'The gentleman attends to the root; when the root is established, the Way grows. Filial piety and fraternal duty, are they not the root of humaneness?' (君子务本，本立而道生。孝弟也者，其为仁之本与).
story.zh: 《论语·学而》：“君子务本，本立而道生。孝弟也者，其为仁之本与！”

usage.en: Formal; often an aphorism on fundamentals. Predicate or quotation.
usage.zh: 书面语，常作格言，谈根本与基础。

natural: filial, brotherly and diligent in farming

meaning.en: Filial duty, brotherly respect and hard farming; in Han times a title and official category used to reward model villagers.
meaning.zh: 孝顺父母、友爱兄弟、努力耕作；汉代用以表彰乡里模范的科目。

examples.zh: 汉代设孝悌力田之科，选拔乡里的品行端正者。
examples.en: The Han dynasty set up the 'filial, fraternal and field-working' category to select upright villagers.

examples.zh: 族谱里记着先人孝悌力田的家风。
examples.en: The genealogy records the ancestors' family tradition of filial duty, brotherly love and diligent farming.

usage.en: Used mainly in historical contexts; 悌 is read tì. Positive.
usage.zh: 多用于历史语境；“悌”读 tì，含褒义。

natural: the three-year mourning period

meaning.en: The Confucian rule that a son mourns his parent for three years (in practice twenty-five or twenty-seven months).
meaning.zh: 儒家规定子女为父母守丧三年（实际为二十五或二十七个月）的礼制。

examples.zh: 宰我曾质疑三年之丧太久，被孔子批评。
examples.en: Zai Wo once questioned whether three years of mourning was too long and was rebuked by Confucius.

examples.zh: 三年之丧的礼制在历史上时紧时松。
examples.en: The three-year mourning rule was enforced strictly in some periods and loosely in others.

examples.zh: 按古礼，父母去世要守孝三年，不婚不仕。
examples.en: By old custom, a child mourned a parent for three years, neither marrying nor taking office.

story.en: Zai Wo asked whether one year of mourning would suffice. Confucius said that a child is cradled for three years after birth, hence 'the three-year mourning is the common rule of the world' (三年之丧，天下之通丧也).
story.zh: 《论语·阳货》：“子生三年，然后免于父母之怀。夫三年之丧，天下之通丧也。”

usage.en: A historical-ritual term, used in discussing Confucian rites. Also called 守孝三年 in plainer speech.
usage.zh: 属礼制史用语；口语也说“守孝三年”。

natural: observe the mourning regulations

meaning.en: In imperial China, for an official to leave office to mourn a parent's death, normally for 27 months.
meaning.zh: 旧时官员遭父母之丧，须辞官回家守孝，一般为二十七个月。

equivalents: leave office to mourn a parent

examples.zh: 张居正当年因父亲去世本应丁忧守制，却被皇帝夺情留任。
examples.en: When Zhang Juzheng's father died he should have left office to mourn, but the emperor kept him in post.

examples.zh: 清代官员丁忧守制期间不得应试或做官。
examples.en: In the Qing, officials in mourning could neither sit exams nor hold office.

usage.en: Historical term; also 丁忧 alone. The reverse, being recalled from mourning, is 夺情.
usage.zh: 历史用语，也可单说“丁忧”；被皇帝召回称“夺情”。

natural: the sigh at the captured qilin

meaning.en: Confucius's sorrow when a qilin was caught and killed, taken as a sign that his Way would not prevail; used for lament at the end of an era or at a hopeless cause.
meaning.zh: 孔子见麒麟被捕获而哀叹，以为是自己主张不行的征兆；后用来比喻对时世衰败、事业无望的哀叹。

examples.zh: 老学者看着传统技艺失传，发出获麟之叹。
examples.en: The old scholar watched the traditional craft die out and lamented it as an age's end.

examples.zh: 文中的获麟之叹，写的是作者对理想破灭的悲伤。
examples.en: The lament over the qilin in the essay expresses the author's grief at shattered ideals.

story.en: In 481 BCE a qilin was caught in the hunt at Daye and killed. Confucius wept: 'My Way is at an end!' and stopped writing the Spring and Autumn Annals.
story.zh: 《春秋》止于“西狩获麟”。《公羊传》载孔子曰：“吾道穷矣！”

usage.en: Literary; allusive. Also used as the traditional end-marker of the Spring and Autumn Annals (see 西狩获麟).
usage.zh: 书面语，用典；参见“西狩获麟”。

natural: a hunt in the west captured a qilin

meaning.en: The event in 481 BCE that closes the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a qilin was captured; by extension, a sign of an era ending or of a work's close.
meaning.zh: 鲁哀公十四年西狩捕获麒麟，《春秋》记事至此而止；后借指一个时代的终结或著述的结束。

examples.zh: 《春秋》终于西狩获麟，因此后人称它为“绝笔”。
examples.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals ends with the capture of the qilin, which is why it is called Confucius's last writing.

examples.zh: 研究者把西狩获麟看作孔子晚年的心理转折点。
examples.en: Scholars view the capture of the qilin as a psychological turning-point for Confucius in old age.

story.en: The final entry of the Spring and Autumn Annals reads 'In the spring of the fourteenth year of Duke Ai, a hunt in the west captured a qilin' (十有四年春，西狩获麟).
story.zh: 《春秋·哀公十四年》：“十有四年春，西狩获麟。”

usage.en: Scholarly allusion; for the personal sorrow itself use 获麟之叹.
usage.zh: 学术典故；表现哀叹之情则用“获麟之叹”。

natural: the wise man withers

meaning.en: A lament for the death of a great and wise person.
meaning.zh: 哀叹贤哲之人逝世。

examples.zh: 先生仙逝，学界同悲，真是哲人其萎。
examples.en: With the master's death the academic world mourns: truly the sage has withered.

examples.zh: 挽联上写着“哲人其萎，风范长存”。
examples.en: The elegiac couplet reads: 'The wise man has withered, his example lives on.'

story.en: Before his death, Confucius sang: 'Mount Tai crumbles! The beam breaks! The wise man withers!' (泰山其颓乎！梁木其坏乎！哲人其萎乎！).
story.zh: 《礼记·檀弓上》：“泰山其颓乎！梁木其坏乎！哲人其萎乎！”

usage.en: Used in obituaries and elegies; formal and solemn, never for the living.
usage.zh: 用于悼词、挽联，庄重书面语，不用于在世者。

pinyin: wú dào yī yǐ guàn zhī
literal: my · Way · one · to · thread · it
natural: my Way is threaded by a single thread

meaning.en: Confucius's remark that all his teaching is bound together by one principle; quoted for a single unifying idea running through one's work or beliefs.
meaning.zh: 孔子说自己的学说有一个根本思想贯穿始终；后用来指有一条主线贯穿始终的思想或做法。

equivalents: one thread runs through it all

examples.zh: “吾道一以贯之”，他的全部研究都围绕着同一个问题。
examples.en: 'My Way is threaded by one'; all his research revolves around a single question.

examples.zh: 这位导演的作品风格各异，却是吾道一以贯之，主题始终是家庭。
examples.en: This director's films differ in style, yet one thread runs through them all: family.

story.en: Confucius said: 'Zeng Shen, my Way is threaded by one'. Zeng answered 'Yes'; afterwards he explained to the others that the Master's Way is loyalty and reciprocity (忠恕).
story.zh: 《论语·里仁》：“参乎！吾道一以贯之。”曾子曰：“唯。”……曾子曰：“夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。”

usage.en: The idiom 一以贯之 (already a headword) comes from this line.曾子 explains the 'one' as loyalty and reciprocity (忠恕).
usage.zh: 成语“一以贯之”即出此句；曾子解释这个“一”是忠恕之道。

pinyin: jìng guǐ shén ér yuǎn zhī
literal: respect · spirits · and · keep distance · from them
natural: respect the spirits but keep your distance

meaning.en: Confucius's advice to treat spirits with respect without getting entangled in them; today quoted for a respectful but detached attitude to anything one should not meddle with.
meaning.zh: 孔子对待鬼神的态度：尊敬而不亲近；今泛指对某事物保持敬重但不过分接近。

examples.zh: 对宗教问题，他一向敬鬼神而远之。
examples.en: On religious matters he has always kept a respectful distance.

examples.zh: 对这类权贵，我们只能敬鬼神而远之。
examples.en: With powerful people of this sort we can only keep a polite distance.

story.en: Fan Chi asked about wisdom. Confucius: 'Devote yourself to what is right for the people, and respect the spirits while keeping them at a distance: this may be called wisdom' (务民之义，敬鬼神而远之，可谓知矣).
story.zh: 《论语·雍也》：“务民之义，敬鬼神而远之，可谓知矣。”

usage.en: Now often humorous when applied to troublesome people or things; the original is neutral to positive.
usage.zh: 今多带戏谑，用于不愿招惹的人或事；本义为中性偏褒。

natural: cut flesh from one's thigh to cure a parent

meaning.en: In old China, to cut flesh from one's own thigh as medicine for a sick parent, regarded as the extreme of filial devotion; now criticised as harmful superstition.
meaning.zh: 旧时子女割下自己大腿的肉给病重的父母做药，被视为孝行极致；今天多视为愚昧自残。

examples.zh: 古书里有不少割股疗亲的故事，今人读来只觉得残忍而不可取。
examples.en: Old books contain many tales of children cutting their flesh to cure a parent, which readers today find cruel and unadvisable.

examples.zh: 割股疗亲并不能治病，反而反映了旧时医疗的无奈。
examples.en: Cutting flesh for a parent does not cure anything; it only reflects the helplessness of old medicine.

usage.en: Historical; modern writers treat it critically. Compare 割肉奉母 and the 二十四孝 stories.
usage.zh: 属历史用语，今人多持批判态度。

natural: what does Heaven say?

meaning.en: Heaven does not speak, yet the seasons turn and all things grow; used to say that the greatest forces work in silence and deeds speak louder than words.
meaning.zh: 天不说话，四季照样运行，万物照样生长；比喻最有力的作用是无言的，行动胜过言语。

examples.zh: “天何言哉”，真正的教育往往是润物无声的。
examples.en: 'What does Heaven say?' True education often works quietly, like rain that moistens without a sound.

examples.zh: 他不爱解释，只信天何言哉，用成绩说话。
examples.en: He does not like explaining himself, trusting that Heaven says nothing and letting his results speak.

story.en: Confucius said: 'I wish to speak no more.' Zigong asked what the disciples would then pass on. Confucius: 'Does Heaven speak? The four seasons run their course, and all things grow. Does Heaven speak?' (天何言哉？四时行焉，百物生焉，天何言哉).
story.zh: 《论语·阳货》：“天何言哉？四时行焉，百物生焉，天何言哉？”

usage.en: Literary; written as a rhetorical question. The same phrase can express resignation.
usage.zh: 书面语，是反问句式，有时也含无可奈何之意。

pinyin: shí bù yán, qǐn bù yǔ
literal: eating · not · talk, · sleeping · not · speak
natural: no talking while eating, no chatting in bed

meaning.en: A table manner and health rule attributed to Confucius: do not talk while eating or when lying down to sleep.
meaning.zh: 相传为孔子的饮食起居规矩：吃饭时不说话，睡觉时不说话。

equivalents: silence at table and in bed

examples.zh: 老一辈人讲究食不言，寝不语，吃饭时孩子们不许说话。
examples.en: The older generation insisted on no talking while eating, so children were not allowed to speak at meals.

examples.zh: 食不言，寝不语，其实对消化和睡眠都有好处。
examples.en: Not talking while eating or in bed is in fact good for digestion and sleep.

story.en: The 'Xiangdang' chapter records Confucius's daily habits, including that 'he did not talk while eating and did not speak in bed' (食不语，寝不言).
story.zh: 《论语·乡党》载孔子日常起居，其中有“食不语，寝不言”，后世常说作“食不言，寝不语”。

usage.en: Often quoted in family-manners talk; chunk form has no comma but the original has one. Both halves are usually quoted together.
usage.zh: 常在谈家教、餐桌礼仪时引用，两句通常连用。

natural: his joy unchanged

meaning.en: To keep one's contentment even in poverty and hardship, as Yan Hui did.
meaning.zh: 身处贫困艰苦的境地，仍保持原有的乐趣和志向。

examples.zh: 住在陋巷，吃粗茶淡饭，他却不改其乐。
examples.en: He lived in a back alley on plain fare, yet his cheerfulness was unchanged.

examples.zh: 再苦再累，她也不改其乐。
examples.en: However hard and tiring, she never lost her joy.

story.en: Confucius on Yan Hui: 'A bowl of rice, a gourd of water, in a mean alley; others could not bear such sorrow, but Hui does not change his joy. How worthy is Hui!' (人不堪其忧，回也不改其乐).
story.zh: 《论语·雍也》：“一箪食，一瓢饮，在陋巷，人不堪其忧，回也不改其乐。贤哉回也！”

usage.en: Positive; usually follows 人不堪其忧 ('others could not bear such misery'), referring to Yan Hui's ideal.
usage.zh: 含褒义，常与“人不堪其忧”连用，指颜回的境界。

pinyin: cún tiān lǐ, miè rén yù
literal: preserve · Heavenly principle, · extinguish · human desires
natural: preserve Heavenly principle, extinguish human desire

meaning.en: The Neo-Confucian (Cheng–Zhu) ethical slogan: keep to moral principle and suppress selfish desires; later widely criticised as repressive.
meaning.zh: 宋明理学的伦理主张：保存天理，消除私欲；后世常被批评为禁欲、压抑人性。

examples.zh: “存天理，灭人欲”在现代人看来过于苛刻。
examples.en: 'Preserve Heavenly principle, extinguish human desire' strikes modern readers as too severe.

examples.zh: 戴震批评宋儒存天理，灭人欲，是“以理杀人”。
examples.en: Dai Zhen criticised the Song Confucians' 'preserve principle, extinguish desire' as 'killing people with principle'.

story.en: Zhu Xi (1130–1200) taught that 'the sages' thousand words come down to teaching people to illuminate Heavenly principle and extinguish human desire' (圣贤千言万语，只是教人明天理，灭人欲); the shortened slogan became a byword of Cheng–Zhu Neo-Confucianism.
story.zh: 朱熹《朱子语类》卷十二：“圣贤千言万语，只是教人明天理，灭人欲。”后简作“存天理，灭人欲”。

usage.en: Historical-philosophical; the 'desires' meant are selfish or excessive ones, but the line has often been taken as against all desire. Frequently quoted critically.
usage.zh: 属思想史用语，原指去除私欲或过度的欲望，但常被理解为否定一切欲望，多用于批评语境。

natural: loyal to the ruler and love the country

meaning.en: Loyalty to the sovereign and love for one's country, the traditional virtue of the loyal official.
meaning.zh: 忠于君主，热爱国家；旧时的臣子美德。

examples.zh: 岳飞以忠君爱国闻名，“精忠报国”四字刻在背上。
examples.en: Yue Fei was famed for loyalty to ruler and country; the four words 'serve the country with utmost loyalty' were tattooed on his back.

examples.zh: 今天我们讲爱国，不必再讲忠君爱国那一套。
examples.en: Today when we speak of patriotism we no longer need the old creed of loyalty to the monarch.

usage.en: Historical flavour: the 'ruler' element is dated, so modern writing prefers 爱国. Positive in tone for historical heroes.
usage.zh: 带历史色彩，“忠君”已过时，现代多说“爱国”；用于历史人物时含褒义。

natural: self-cultivation, family, state and world

meaning.en: Short for 修身、齐家、治国、平天下: cultivating oneself, ordering the family, governing the state and bringing peace to the world; the Confucian ladder of ambition.
meaning.zh: “修身、齐家、治国、平天下”的简称，儒家由个人到天下的修养与抱负次第。

examples.zh: 读书人向来以修齐治平为人生目标。
examples.en: Scholars have always taken self-cultivation, family order, good government and world peace as life goals.

examples.zh: 修齐治平，先从修身做起。
examples.en: Of self-cultivation, family, state and world, begin with oneself.

story.en: The Great Learning: 'Cultivated oneself, then the family is regulated; the family regulated, then the state is governed; the state governed, then the world is at peace' (身修而后家齐，家齐而后国治，国治而后天下平).
story.zh: 《礼记·大学》：“身修而后家齐，家齐而后国治，国治而后天下平。”

usage.en: A contraction; the full form 修身齐家治国平天下 is also in the dictionary. Formal, aspirational.
usage.zh: 为缩略语，全文为“修身齐家治国平天下”，正式而富抱负色彩。

literal: be humane to · people · cherish · creatures
natural: care for the people and cherish living things

meaning.en: To be benevolent to people and cherish living things and the environment; for Mencius, a widening circle of compassion.
meaning.zh: 对人仁爱，对万物爱惜；孟子所说的由亲及人再及物的仁爱之心。

equivalents: love humanity and cherish living things

examples.zh: 他提倡仁民爱物，从保护河流和老人做起。
examples.en: He advocates caring for both people and nature, from protecting rivers to looking after the elderly.

examples.zh: 仁民爱物的思想对今天的环保仍有启发。
examples.en: The idea of benevolence to people and things still inspires environmental protection today.

story.en: Mencius: 'The gentleman is affectionate to his kin, then humane to the people; humane to the people, then cherishing to creatures' (亲亲而仁民，仁民而爱物).
story.zh: 《孟子·尽心上》：“君子之于物也，爱之而弗仁；于民也，仁之而弗亲。亲亲而仁民，仁民而爱物。”

usage.en: Formal and positive; often used for ecological ethics. Predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 正式褒义，常用于生态伦理，可作谓语、定语。

natural: the Mandate of Heaven is not constant

meaning.en: Heaven's mandate to rule does not stay with any one house; it passes to whoever rules with virtue. Used of fortunes and dynasties that rise and fall.
meaning.zh: 上天赐予的统治之命不会永远属于一家一姓，有德者得之；比喻兴衰无常。

examples.zh: 王朝更替，天命靡常，只有施行仁政才能长久。
examples.en: Dynasties change; the Mandate is not constant, and only benevolent rule can last.

examples.zh: 企业今天风光明天落魄，真是天命靡常。
examples.en: A company is glorious today and ruined tomorrow; truly, nothing is permanent.

story.en: The Zhou hymn 'King Wen' says that Heaven's mandate is not constant, so Yin's descendants, once glorious, had to submit to Zhou (侯服于周，天命靡常).
story.zh: 《诗经·大雅·文王》：“侯服于周，天命靡常。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Literary and political; 靡 means 'not' (无). Pairs with 以德配天.
usage.zh: 书面语，政治色彩；“靡”意为“无”，与“以德配天”相关。

natural: match Heaven through virtue

meaning.en: A ruler's virtue must be great enough to deserve Heaven's mandate; the Zhou idea that legitimacy rests on moral worth.
meaning.zh: 统治者的德行要足以配得上天命；周代提出的政权合法性取决于道德的观念。

equivalents: rule must be earned by virtue

examples.zh: 周公提出以德配天，开启了中国政治思想的新传统。
examples.en: The Duke of Zhou's idea that virtue matches Heaven began a new tradition in Chinese political thought.

examples.zh: 古人认为君主必须以德配天，否则会失去天命。
examples.en: The ancients held that a monarch must match Heaven with virtue or lose the mandate.

usage.en: Formal; political-philosophical. Often with 天命靡常.
usage.zh: 正式用语，政治哲学色彩，常与“天命靡常”并说。

natural: good deeds leave surplus blessings

meaning.en: A family that piles up good deeds will have blessings left over for its descendants.
meaning.zh: 积累善行的人家，必然有福泽留给子孙。

examples.zh: 积善余庆，他们家几代行善，子孙也都有出息。
examples.en: Good deeds leave blessings: their family did good for generations and the descendants all prospered.

examples.zh: 老人常说积善余庆，劝我们多做好事。
examples.en: The old man often says that good deeds bring blessings and urges us to do more of them.

story.en: The commentary on the Kun hexagram says: 'A house that accumulates good will surely have surplus blessings; a house that accumulates evil will surely have surplus calamity' (积善之家，必有余庆；积不善之家，必有余殃).
story.zh: 《周易·坤·文言》：“积善之家，必有余庆；积不善之家，必有余殃。”

date.zh: 西周至战国 · 前9—前3世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Warring States, 9th–3rd c. BC

usage.en: Usually in the saying 积善之家，必有余庆 and its counterpart 积不善之家，必有余殃. Sometimes used to console.
usage.zh: 常见于“积善之家，必有余庆”，其对句为“积不善之家，必有余殃”。

natural: Confucius's mat never grew warm

meaning.en: Confucius never stayed in one place long enough to warm his seat, always travelling to spread his ideas; used of someone constantly on the move for a cause.
meaning.zh: 孔子为推行主张四处奔走，坐席还没暖热就又起身；形容为事业而奔波忙碌。

equivalents: always on the road for a cause

examples.zh: 为了公益事业，他一年到头孔席不暖。
examples.en: For his charity work he is on the road all year without rest.

examples.zh: 孔席不暖，墨突不黔，说的就是圣贤为天下奔走。
examples.en: 'Confucius's mat never warm, Mozi's chimney never black' describes sages rushing about for the world's sake.

story.en: Ban Gu wrote: 'Confucius's mat was never warm, Mozi's chimney was never black' (孔席不暇暖，墨突不得黔), meaning the sages were too busy to rest.
story.zh: 班固《答宾戏》：“孔席不暖，墨突不黔。”

usage.en: Positive and literary; usually paired with 墨突不黔. Note 暖 here is nuǎn.
usage.zh: 褒义书面语，常与“墨突不黔”连用。

natural: Mencius's mother cut her weaving

meaning.en: When young Mencius skipped school, his mother cut the cloth on her loom to show that abandoning study halfway is as wasteful; used for strict, wise parental teaching.
meaning.zh: 孟子少时逃学，孟母割断织布，以示半途而废的后果；比喻母亲教子有方、严格督促。

equivalents: cut the cloth to teach a lesson

examples.zh: 妈妈用孟母断织的故事鼓励我坚持学业。
examples.en: Mum used the story of Mencius's mother cutting her weaving to urge me to keep studying.

examples.zh: 孟母断织与孟母三迁，都说明了家教的重要。
examples.en: Mencius's mother cutting the cloth and moving house thrice both show the importance of upbringing.

story.en: In Liu Xiang's Biographies of Exemplary Women, Mencius returns from school early; his mother cuts her cloth and says that stopping study midway is like cutting the weaving.
story.zh: 西汉刘向《列女传·母仪》载：孟子辍学而归，孟母以刀断其织，曰：“子之废学，若吾断斯织也。”

usage.en: Allusion often paired with 孟母三迁. Positive; the point is perseverance in study.
usage.zh: 典故，常与“孟母三迁”并称，含褒义，重点是学习要持之以恒。
